<!-- pr-reviewer: 2e9cdb06ccb4cfa4bbfc016493440264da5f3dc5 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

Judged against #1185's "Done means": a re-import defaults to the budget recorded with the model, the user can still change it, a test pins it, and the MCP and script re-imports do the same. All of that holds.

### What looks good
- One resolver, `model_fidelity::reimport_budget` (crates/app/src/model_fidelity.rs:84). The GUI (`state_step_budget.rs` `step_budget_for`), the script verb (`script/api.rs:63-66`) and MCP `import_model` (it forwards to `v_import`) all use it. Nothing is duplicated.
- The budget, mesh and flag stay consistent with each other by construction. The resolved budget goes into `ImportModel::within`. The mesh, `coarse_mm` and the recorded `facet_budget` all come out of that one call, and `UpdateModel` then gets `.with_fidelity(imp.coarse_mm).with_budget(imp.facet_budget)`. A model can't be re-meshed coarse and still be flagged full fidelity. The MCP test checks this (`reduced_fidelity` is present on the kept 2000-facet re-import), and so does the UI test (`flags()` compares budget and chord).
- Edge cases fall back safely:
  - Old projects with no `StepBudget`, or a default budget: the import uses the default, the same as before.
  - A hand-edited recorded budget out of bounds: `budget_of` filters it through `step_budget::check`, so the import uses the default and is never refused deep inside.
  - An STL or OBJ path: never picks up a recorded budget.
  - A STEP file that grew since import: the recorded budget coarsens it, and the model is flagged reduced fidelity. Nothing passes silently.
- An explicit budget still wins on every path (the GUI's committed setting, `facet_budget` on MCP, the third arg on script). The re-import is still the existing undoable `UpdateModel`, so undo and the out-of-date marking of dependent operations work as before.
- No verb renamed or removed. `cam.import` keeps its signature, and the name argument is now read once, before the budget is resolved. No project-format change. No snapshot PNGs, process files or `CHANGELOG.md` touched. No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` (`unwrap_or("model")` matches `ImportModel`'s own naming). ui -> app layering is kept.
- The decision note is in `docs/decisions/1185-reimport-budget.md`. Conventional subject, `Changelog:` line, `Fixes #1185`.

### Local results (trial-merged with main 2bc79a3c, clean merge)
| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| camcraft-app lib | 147 passed |
| app `step_budget` | 6 passed |
| app `model_fidelity` | 9 passed |
| app `coarse_laws` | 6 passed |
| app `step_fidelity` | 2 passed |
| app `import` | 26 passed |
| app `project_roundtrip` | 71 passed |
| app `scripting` | 18 passed |
| app `mcp_model` | 5 passed |
| camcraft-ui lib (CWD `crates/ui`) | 616 passed, 5 ignored |
| clippy `-p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -D warnings` | clean |

I also ran a throwaway local probe (not pushed), and both cases passed:
- A script calls `cam.import(p, null, 2000)` and then `cam.import(p)`. The second import keeps 2000 and stays flagged.
- A recorded budget of 5 (out of bounds) resolves to the default.

### Requested before merge
None.

### Notes (not blocking)
1. In the GUI, once a budget is committed it is "explicit" for the rest of the session (`state_step_budget.rs:55`). Every later STEP re-import of any model then uses it, not that model's recorded budget, and the only way back is a restart. The decision note says this is on purpose, and the model page does show the next-import value, so it is not silent. A small "use the model's recorded budget" reset could come later.
2. The new row line "A re-import keeps N unless a budget is set below" (`step_budget_row.rs:20-22`) also shows on STL/OBJ and box models, where a budget never applies. No test asserts it, and the status line in `begin_import` isn't asserted either. A structural assertion for the row text would help.
3. `crates/ui/src/state.rs` is about 4,360 lines and this PR adds 3. The growth is small, but the status-line text could live in `state_step_budget.rs` beside `step_budget_for`.
4. The status line "importing X under its recorded STEP facet budget of N…" is overwritten by the "updated X" message when the import finishes. On a fast import the user may never see which budget was used.

Not exercised: the GUI by hand, and a real large STEP file (only the `Milling-test.step` fixture was used).

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
